A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EnvInjection study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success experiments across ten webpage datasets and five MLLM-based agents, including detailed appendix results and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds computational-cost results in Appendix Table 12.

M1.justification: The constrained optimization objective, U-Net mapping surrogate, differentiable resizing, PGD updates, and webpage-code implementation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same real and synthetic webpages across five categories, with the same monitor, paraphrased-prompt, and alternative-action scenarios. The added cost comparison introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Naive, Context Ignoring, Fake Completion, Combined, and Screenshot-based attacks. Table 12 reuses the screenshot-based comparator. Dropping Wu et al. from the baseline paragraph does not establish a change to the reported comparator or implementation.

E3.justification: Table 12 adds training-time and GPU-memory evaluation per target webpage per target monitor on one RTX A6000. Existing ASR evaluation, model configurations, prompt/history sampling, and optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 12 adds an efficiency analysis of EnvInjection's computational overhead relative to screenshot-based attacks. Existing monitor-count, perturbation-bound, prompt-variant, and alternative-action analyses are retained. The new defense discussion contains no defense experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added computational-cost results also lack uncertainty estimates; existing averaging practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The ASR values in Tables 1 and 4–11 and the plotted result curves are unchanged. New Table 12 reports additional training time of 1.70–2.57 minutes and memory usage of 1.93–2.61 GB above screenshot-based attacks, depending on the agent.

T1.justification: Formal assumptions and mathematical formulations are retained. v2's newly numbered Equation 2 restates v1's inline loss, and its reformatted ASR equation is algebraically equivalent. No substantive derivation or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an effective, stealthy, practical webpage-based attack using perturbations across selected monitors, with substantially higher attack success than baselines. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds prospective defenses through source-code inspection, perturbation detection, and adversarial training, and argues that DataSentinel does not apply to this nontextual attack. The existing webpage-control and unevaluated closed-model-transfer limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 12 newly discloses RTX A6000 hardware and resource overhead. Existing hyperparameters, monitor-simulation and perturbation code, generation prompts, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially expands positioning through indirect and optimized prompt injection, alignment poisoning, prompt leakage, and tool attacks, citing additional work including Greshake, Hui, Shao, and Shi et al. Section 8 adds defense literature. WIPI is removed, and the Carlini–Wagner reference is replaced by a different 2017 paper.

P1.justification: Limited prose edits accompany reordered and expanded related work, separate Conclusion and Limitations sections, relocation of Algorithm 1 to the appendix, and new acknowledgments. Most background, method, and experimental exposition is retained.

P2.justification: Main text and references change from one to two columns, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures, tables, and code displays. v1 Figures 2 and 3 merge into v2 Figure 2; several perturbation-bound plots gain zero ticks/gridlines, and Table 12 is added.

improvement.justification: Table 12 supplies computational-overhead evidence absent from v1, improving practical transparency. Expanded related work and prospective defenses provide useful context while preserving existing scientific results. The gains are limited: absolute baseline costs remain unspecified, and the proposed defenses are unevaluated.
